headline: Tropical Depression Pilandok Remains Far East of Northern Luzon as Habagat Persists
seoTitle: Tropical Depression Pilandok and Habagat Update | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA placed Tropical Depression Pilandok far east of Extreme Northern Luzon at 5 p.m. August 30, with no wind signal in effect as Habagat hazards persisted.
deck: PAGASA's 5 p.m. bulletin placed Pilandok far east of Extreme Northern Luzon with 45 km/h sustained winds and no tropical cyclone wind signal in effect.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Tropical Depression Pilandok remained over the Philippine Sea far east of Extreme Northern Luzon on Sunday afternoon while the Southwest Monsoon continued to affect parts of the country, according to PAGASA's 5 p.m. bulletin.

At 4 p.m., PAGASA estimated the center about 1,180 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon. Pilandok had maximum sustained winds of 45 kilometers per hour, gusts of up to 55 km/h and was moving northwestward slowly.

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: The bulletin email carried earlier formation-stage estimates of 55 km/h sustained winds, a position 460 kilometers east-northeast of Aparri and Signal No. 1 over Batanes and the Babuyan Islands. Those details were not carried into this update because PAGASA's later official bulletin placed the cyclone much farther east and showed no tropical cyclone wind signal in effect.
PAGASA said Pilandok was less likely to make landfall and was expected to remain a tropical depression before weakening into a remnant low over the Philippine Sea south of Japan on Tuesday.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: PAGASA directed readers to its separate Southwest Monsoon advisory for the heavy-rainfall outlook. The cyclone bulletin warned of strong to gale-force monsoon gusts over many areas and rough seas reaching four meters along the western seaboard of the Babuyan Islands.
This update continues the developing weather event on FMB News' established canonical route and removes a separate route created from the same sequence.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Cyclone position, intensity and warning signals can change substantially within hours. Residents and mariners should use the newest PAGASA products rather than relying on earlier estimates reproduced in social posts or bulletins.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch PAGASA's succeeding tropical cyclone bulletins, rainfall advisories and local disaster instructions for changes in Pilandok's track and the continuing effects of the Southwest Monsoon.
